A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayesian Sample Inference work. The complete main texts, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original BSI experiments on ImageNet32, ImageNet64 and CIFAR10, including likelihoods, sample quality and parameter studies in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original BSI experiments and parameter studies. Although some CIFAR10 baseline scores are explicitly attributed to prior work, the paper's own experimental results clearly qualify.

M1.justification: The posterior updates, BSI prior, training objective, sampling algorithm, preconditioning and backbone choices remain unchanged. Algorithm 2's corrected output label matches its existing return expression. The newly specified sampling schedule documents the procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10, ImageNet32 and ImageNet64 for image likelihood evaluation and unconditional generation. Newly discussed high-resolution, non-image and discrete domains are possible extensions, not added evaluations.

E2.justification: BFN and VDM remain the comparators in the corresponding ImageNet, U-Net and CIFAR10 comparisons. Posterior Mean Matching and Sequential Monte Carlo methods are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the stated conversion to bits from multiplication by log(2) to division by log(2), and corrects the discrete Normal upper-bin boundary. These revise the documented likelihood calculation; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Existing datasets, budgets, sample counts and evaluation procedures otherwise match.

E4.justification: The ELBO convergence, variance reduction, proposal-distribution check, architecture comparison, initial-precision sweep and finite-versus-infinite-step training studies are retained in Section 6, Figures 4–8 and Table 3. No new ablation or robustness analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly identifies its uncertainties as standard deviations over three seeds; v3 supplied the same uncertainty values without that specification. Section 6.2 clarifies that CIFAR10 uses one model per training budget. Neither change establishes an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their scores, including BSI FIDs of 8.9 ± 0.1 on ImageNet32 and 30.1 ± 0.4 on ImageNet64. Plotted values, error bars and generated samples also match. Appendix E's added images-per-hour figures convert previously reported step rates and batch sizes.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 corrects the denoiser loss's linear term from the belief mean to the true sample. Appendix B fixes the bit conversion and bin boundary, and Appendix D.6 corrects noise signs. Lemma 3.3 and its proof make strict schedule-refinement monotonicity explicit, building on v3's existing argument. The central ELBO results are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion distinguish the general Bayesian framework from BSI: BSI and BFN occupy opposite hyper-prior extremes, replacing statements that BSI itself includes BFN. The headline sample-quality claim now explicitly includes ImageNet64, whose supporting results already appeared in v3.

C2.justification: New Section 7.1 identifies limits concerning image resolution, model scale and untested modalities. Section 6 clarifies that the BFN comparison reflects both hyper-prior randomness and initial precision, and restricts Figure 3's advantage to at least 16 steps. Section 5.3 describes the chosen initial precision as balancing likelihood and sample quality rather than optimizing both.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 newly specifies the inverse-CDF sampling schedule. Section 6 and Appendix E clarify baseline provenance, shared training settings and compute accounting; Table 5 now includes both already-reported CIFAR10 budgets. The code-access statement additionally advertises a self-contained implementation and interactive notebook.

R1.justification: New Appendices A.4–A.5 provide focused comparisons with Posterior Mean Matching and Sequential Monte Carlo, citing Salazar, Chen and Wu et al. Rombach et al. is added for potential latent-space extensions. Existing BFN, VDM, diffusion and stochastic-interpolant discussions remain, with clearer BSI–BFN positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, prior discussion and conclusion receive focused rewrites, with terminology and prose corrections throughout. Limitations, broader impact and two related-work subsections are added, while the overall Sections 1–7 and Appendices A–F organization is retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from two columns to a single-column TMLR layout, changing typography, author and publication headers, algorithm placement and figure/table arrangement. Captions gain clarifications, and Figures 7–8 are resized while preserving their plotted evidence. This is a substantial document-wide visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects concrete mathematical errors in the denoiser-loss and discrete-likelihood explanations, clarifies the relationship between BSI and its broader framework, and improves sampling documentation, uncertainty attribution and limitations. These strengthen correctness and reproducibility within the existing study; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
